status_note: Reproduces on Spark 4.3.0 in both ANSI modes, interpreted and codegen. SPARK-45438 (open since 2023, Scala 2.13 builds) reports the raise for `-x` and `abs(x)` at the largest 38-digit decimal; the silent rounding of any decimal past 34 significant digits is the same cause and is not in it. Source at v4.3.0 (98bc0212): `Decimal.unary_-` still negates the Scala `BigDecimal`, whose `MathContext` is `DECIMAL128`.
summary: `-x` and `abs(x)` of a `DECIMAL` with more than 34 significant digits round it half up to 34 digits, silently: `-CAST('12345678901234567890123456789012345678' AS DECIMAL(38,0))` is -12345678901234567890123456789012350000. `0 - x` is exact.

At 10³⁸ - 1 the rounding reaches 10³⁸, which does not fit `DECIMAL(38,0)`, so `-x` raises `NUMERIC_VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE` even with ANSI off. `Decimal.unary_-` (sql/api/.../types/Decimal.scala#L567-L575) builds `-decimalVal` on a Scala `BigDecimal`, which rounds to its default `MathContext.DECIMAL128` (34 digits); `abs` calls it.
handling: The Spark profile (#739) should spell `negate` of a decimal as `0 - x` and `abs` as `CASE WHEN x < 0 THEN 0 - x ELSE x END`. The fix upstream is to negate the Java `BigDecimal` (`decimalVal.underlying.negate()`), which is exact.
found_by: the Spark characterization (#738): sverify_dev.probe_spark, then a manual repro of `decimal-overflow-subtract`
